---
title: "Output files"
---

The script writes everything to the `output` folder.

| file | rows | what it is |
|---|---:|---|
| [`event.csv`](output/event.csv) | 60 | one survey event and 59 photo events |
| [`occurrence.csv`](output/occurrence.csv) | 106 | one taxon in one photo |
| [`extendedmeasurementorfact.csv`](output/extendedmeasurementorfact.csv) | 601 | cover, point counts, and quadrat details |
| [`meta.xml`](output/meta.xml) | — | the Darwin Core Archive descriptor |
| [`README.txt`](output/README.txt) | — | a short note for the archive |
| [`p2p-azores-2026.zip`](output/p2p-azores-2026.zip) | — | all files together |

The zip file is ready to upload to the IPT.

## What is in each table?

### Events

The first row is the parent event for the survey.
The other 59 rows are the photo events.
Each photo event has its own latitude and longitude.

### Occurrences

Each row is one taxon in one photo.
The row has the scientific name, the AphiaID, the percent cover, and the person or machine that identified it.

### Measurements

The eMoF table has seven kinds of measurement:

| measurement | rows | unit |
|---|---:|---|
| quadrat area | 59 | square metres |
| camera height above substrate | 59 | centimetres |
| number of points classified as non-taxon | 59 | counts |
| percent cover | 106 | percent |
| number of points | 106 | counts |
| machine-annotated points | 106 | counts |
| human-annotated points | 106 | counts |

## A first look at the occurrences

```{r}
#| echo: false
occ <- read.csv("output/occurrence.csv", colClasses = "character",
                check.names = FALSE)
first <- occ[1:10, c(
  "scientificName", "organismQuantity", "basisOfRecord", "identifiedBy"
)]
print(first, row.names = FALSE)
```

## The archive

The zip file contains:

- `event.csv`
- `occurrence.csv`
- `extendedmeasurementorfact.csv`
- `meta.xml`
- `README.txt`

`meta.xml` tells the IPT which column is which Darwin Core term.
The column order in the CSV files must match `meta.xml`.
The script writes both, so they stay in step.

::: {.callout-note}
The script does not make EML.
Add the dataset title, abstract, methods, and licence in the IPT.
:::
